subject: Place a grid.table on defined coordinates on top of a ggplot?

messages.author: 409dfe1554e9c224
messages.subject: Place a grid.table on defined coordinates on top of a ggplot?
parts:
Hi,

I can overlay a grid.table on a ggplot like so
> library(ggplot2)
> library(gridExtra)
> qplot(mpg, wt, data=mtcars)
> grid.table(head(iris)[c(1,2)])

but how can I shift the table from the plot center to the upper right corner -
possibly with some padding to the coordinate system's border (but this can be
done manually) ?

Thanks for any hints, Joh

messages.author: afa289b81aad98c2
messages.subject: Re: Place a grid.table on defined coordinates on top of a ggplot?
parts:
Jon, in ggExtra there is a geom that will do this. Here's a piece of code I
posted a few days ago that allows the table to be moved around - you can
probably use this as a guide. Or, look at the page for ggExtra and
Geom_Table info.

Bryan
*************
Bryan Hanson
Professor of Chemistry & Biochemistry
DePauw University, Greencastle IN USA

rxnNorm <- function(data = NULL, res = NULL,
fac1 = NULL, fac2 = NULL, fac2cols = NULL,
freckles = FALSE, type = c("connect", "fitLine"),
method = c("sem", "iqr", "mad", "box", "sem95"),
table = NULL, xlab = NULL, ylab = NULL, title = NULL, ...) {

# Function to compare categorical data by
# plotting means etc in the same panel
# Option to connect the dots or do a fit
# Bryan Hanson, DePauw Univ, July 2010

# Both fac1 and fac2 must be given: this is G x E!
# fac2 must be a factor, but fac1 can be either factor or numeric
# Everything related to a particular level of fac2 should be colored the
same

require(ggplot2)
require(ChemoSpec) # on GitHub
require(plyr)
require(ggExtra)

if (is.null(fac2cols)) stop("You need to supply fac2cols")

# 1st, reduce the df and clean it of NAs
# otherwise there is trouble with the counts
# plus this keeps the ggplot2 object size down

keep <- c(res, fac1, fac2)
data <- data[, keep]
data <- na.omit(data)

# Specify the data & aesthetics

p <- ggplot(data, aes_string(x = fac1, y = res, color = fac2,
group = fac2))

# now add layers as requested

if (freckles) {
jit <- position_jitter(width = 0.05, height = 0.0)
p <- p + geom_jitter(position = jit, size = 1.0)
}

if (method == "box") { # this doesn't work right
p <- p + geom_boxplot(width = 0.2)
if (type == "connect") {
p <- p + stat_summary(fun.y = "median", geom = "line")
}
}

if (method == "sem") {
p <- p + stat_summary(fun.data = "seXy")
if (type == "connect") {
p <- p + stat_summary(fun.y = "mean", geom = "line")
}
}

if (method == "sem95") {
p <- p + stat_summary(fun.data = "seXy95")
if (type == "connect") {
p <- p + stat_summary(fun.y = "mean", geom = "line")
}
}

if (method == "mad") {
p <- p + stat_summary(fun.data = "seXyMad")
if (type == "connect") {
p <- p + stat_summary(fun.y = "median", geom = "line")
}
}

if (method == "iqr") {
p <- p + stat_summary(fun.data = "seXyIqr")
if (type == "connect") {
p <- p + stat_summary(fun.y = "median", geom = "line")
}
}

if (type == "fitLine") {
p <- p + geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE)

}

# now add the common decorations & modifications

p <- p + scale_colour_manual(name = "", values = fac2cols) +
opts(axis.text.x = theme_text(colour = "black"),
axis.text.y = theme_text(colour = "black"),
axis.ticks = theme_blank()) + opts(...)
# now add labels and fix limits (modified from qplot)

if (!is.null(title)) p <- p + opts(title = title)
if (!is.null(xlab)) p <- p + xlab(xlab)
if (!is.null(ylab)) p <- p + ylab(ylab)
# if (exists("xlim")) p <- p + xlim(xlim)
# if (exists("ylim")) p <- p + ylim(ylim)

# now add summary tables
# using a nice table feature from ggExtra

if (!is.null(table)) {

if (type == "connect") {
counts <- count(data, vars = c(fac2, fac1))
colnames(counts) <- c(fac2, fac1, "count")

p <- p + annotate("table", table[1], table[2], table = counts,
theme = theme.list(show.box = TRUE, separator = "black",
gp = gpar(cex = table[3]),
show.csep = TRUE, show.rsep = TRUE, show.colnames = TRUE,
show.rownames = FALSE))
}

if (type == "fitLine") {
lvls <- levels(data[,fac2])
nl <- length(lvls)
m <- c()
b <- c()
r2 <- c()
for (i in 1:nl) {
dat <- subset(data, data[,fac2] == lvls[i])
mod <- lm(dat[,res] ~ dat[,fac1])
m[i] <- round(mod$coef[2], 2)
b [i]<- round(mod$coef[1], 2)
r2[i] <- round(cor(dat[,fac1], dat[,res])^2, 4)

}

mod.res <- data.frame(line = lvls, m = m, b = b, r2 = r2)

p <- p + annotate("table", table[1], table[2], table = mod.res,
theme = theme.list(show.box = TRUE, separator = "black",
gp = gpar(cex = table[3]),
show.csep = TRUE, show.rsep = TRUE, show.colnames = TRUE,
show.rownames = FALSE))

}
}
invisible(p)

}

messages.subject: Re: Place a grid.table on defined coordinates on top of a ggplot?
parts:
Hi,

Try this (click on the graph where you want the table to be)

grid.table(head(iris)[c(1,2)], vp = do.call(viewport, grid.locator()))

or specify a viewport with x andy positions.

HTH,

baptiste

messages.subject: Re: Place a grid.table on defined coordinates on top of a ggplot?
parts:
Hi,

I'm getting the knack of this. Thanks!

> library(gridExtra)
> library(ggplot2)
> qplot(mpg, wt, data=mtcars)
> seekViewport("panel-3-3")
> pushViewport(viewport(x=1,y=1,width=1/2,height=1/2,just=c("right","top")))
> grid.table(head(mtcars)[c(1,2)])

It would be tremendously helpful in situations like this to be able to say
"just=c("right","top")" in the "grid.table" call, such that the table would
automatically orient itself in the top right corner of the viewport ... is
that feasible?

Thanks, Joh

parts: On Aug 6, 2010, at 3:49 PM, Johannes Graumann wrote:

> Hi,

>> library(gridExtra)
>> library(ggplot2)
>> qplot(mpg, wt, data=mtcars)
>> seekViewport("panel-3-3")
>> pushViewport(viewport(x=1,y=1,width=1/2,height=1/2,just=c("right","top")))
>> grid.table(head(mtcars)[c(1,2)])
>
> It would be tremendously helpful in situations like this to be able to say
> "just=c("right","top")" in the "grid.table" call, such that the table would
> automatically orient itself in the top right corner of the viewport ... is
> that feasible?

I don't see how it would be done without sacrificing the possibility of arbitrary placement. What you could do is create a small function that creates the viewports you want and use these (no need to push a viewport manually, btw),

my.vp <- function(just="topright"){

switch(just,
"topright" = viewport(x=1,y=1,width=1/2,height=1/2,just=c("right","top")),
"botleft" = viewport(x=0,y=0,width=1/2,height=1/2,just=c("left","bottom")),
viewport(x=1,y=1,width=1/2,height=1/2,just=c("right","top")))

}

qplot(mpg, wt, data=mtcars, facets=~gear)
seekViewport("panel-2-2")
grid.table(head(mtcars)[c(1,2)], vp=my.vp("topright"))
seekViewport("panel-6-2")
grid.table(head(mtcars)[c(1,2)], vp=my.vp())
seekViewport("panel-2-5")
grid.table(head(mtcars)[c(1,2)], vp=my.vp("botleft"))

HTH,

baptiste

>>>>
>>>> theme = theme.list(show.box = TRUE, separator = "black",

>>>>

>>>>
